description.value: A multimodal neuroimaging study of heroin-dependent patients examining voxel-wise relationships between gray matter density and cerebral perfusion after heroin and placebo administration using arterial spin labeling, voxel-based morphometry, and Biological Parametric Mapping.

spans.text: Using a double-blind, within-subject design, heroin or placebo (saline) was administered to 14 heroin-dependent patients from a stable heroin-assisted treatment program, in order to observe acute short-term effects.

spans.text: We hypothesized that, within the medial frontal and the temporal cortex, low perfusion should correlates with low GM volume.

description.value: Double-blind, within-subject crossover study in which heroin-dependent out-patients received intravenous heroin or placebo on separate scanning occasions.

spans.text: In a cross-over, double-blind design, placebo (5 ml saline), and half of the daily heroin dose (mean = 176 ± 89.1 mg) were administered intravenously over a period of 30 s by a study nurse 20 min before the scanning session started.

value: Biological Parametric Mapping analysis integrating GM and perfusion data after the placebo treatment revealed a significant positive correlation between perfusion and GM volume in frontal areas on both hemispheres.

spans.text: Biological Parametric Mapping analysis integrating GM and perfusion data after the placebo treatment revealed a significant positive correlation between perfusion and GM volume in frontal areas on both hemispheres including the precentral gyrus, the inferior, middle and superior frontal gyrus, the frontal pole, and the right paracingulate cortex, including parts of the ACC (Table  1  and Figure  2 , upper panel).
In order to restrict our analyses to fronto-temporal regions, that we had found to be hypoperfused during heroin ( 17 ), we used an explicit mask of the frontal and temporal lobe by WFU PickAtlas .

pulse_sequence_type.value: flow-sensitive alternating inversion recovery spin labeling with modified Q2TIPS pulse preparation and single-shot 3D gradient-spin echo readout

spans.text: ASL was based on a flow-sensitive alternating inversion recovery spin labeling scheme ( 25 ), combined with modified Q2TIPS (TI periodic saturation) pulse preparation and a single-shot 3D gradient-spin echo readout ( 26 )

description.value: ASL perfusion maps were calculated from label and control images, converted from MHD to NIFTI, realigned, masked with binarized intracranial tissue, normalized to MNI space, smoothed, and proportionally scaled.

spans.text: in-house software from ASL DICOM data

value: fitting to an ideal flow model

spans.text: The difference images of the label and control images were first calculated and the time course was fitted to an ideal flow model.
smoothed using a 6 mm full-width-at half-maximum (FWHM) Gaussian kernel

description.value: MPRAGE images were processed using VBM in SPM8, including non-rigid DARTEL normalization, gray-matter segmentation and modulation with Jacobian determinants, followed by spatial smoothing.

spans.text: MPRAGE images were non-rigidly normalized to a population-based average using diffeomorphic anatomical registration through exponentiated lie algebra (DARTEL) ( 27 ). The segmented tissue maps of GM were modulated with the Jacobian determinants from the spatial normalization to correct for volume changes. Finally, images were smoothed with an 8 mm FWHM Gaussian kernel.
